title: Filling a Viterbi trellis
sub: Rows are hidden states, columns are days. Each cell keeps only the best path into it, and remembers where it came from.

frames.caption: Three hidden weather states, observed only through whether someone carries an umbrella: umbrella, umbrella, no umbrella, no umbrella. Each cell will hold the probability of the best path ending there.
Day 1, Rainy: start probability 0.5 × P(umbrella | Rainy) 0.9 = 0.450.
Day 1, Cloudy: start probability 0.3 × P(umbrella | Cloudy) 0.5 = 0.150.
Day 1, Sunny: start probability 0.2 × P(umbrella | Sunny) 0.1 = 0.020.
Day 2, Rainy: the best way in is from Rainy (0.450 × 0.6), then × P(umbrella | Rainy) 0.9 = 0.243.
Day 2, Cloudy: the best way in is from Rainy (0.450 × 0.3), then × P(umbrella | Cloudy) 0.5 = 0.068.
Day 2, Sunny: the best way in is from Rainy (0.450 × 0.1), then × P(umbrella | Sunny) 0.1 = 0.005.
Day 3, Rainy: the best way in is from Rainy (0.243 × 0.6), then × P(no umbrella | Rainy) 0.1 = 0.015.
Day 3, Cloudy: the best way in is from Rainy (0.243 × 0.3), then × P(no umbrella | Cloudy) 0.5 = 0.036.
Day 3, Sunny: the best way in is from Rainy (0.243 × 0.1), then × P(no umbrella | Sunny) 0.9 = 0.022.
Day 4, Rainy: the best way in is from Cloudy (0.036 × 0.3), then × P(no umbrella | Rainy) 0.1 = 0.001.
Day 4, Cloudy: the best way in is from Cloudy (0.036 × 0.4), then × P(no umbrella | Cloudy) 0.5 = 0.007.
Day 4, Sunny: the best way in is from Sunny (0.022 × 0.6), then × P(no umbrella | Sunny) 0.9 = 0.012.
The best final cell is Sunny. Follow the stored back-pointers: the most likely weather was Rainy → Rainy → Sunny → Sunny, with probability 0.012.
